I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me not to attend my great aunt's funeral. Let me break this down step by step. First, I just found out about her passing. My mom told me today, and I had never heard of her before. The only time I met her was when I was a baby, like 1 or 2 years old. So, I don't really have any memories or connection with her. That makes me feel a bit disconnected from the situation. My mom is insisting I go to the funeral. She says it's out of respect and to support her. But I'm really awkward at funerals, especially for people I don't know well. I mean, I've been to a few funerals, but they were for people I knew better. Going to one for someone I barely know feels strange. It's like gate-crashing, even though I'm family. She also mentioned that it's a chance to meet a larger branch of the family. There might be hundreds of people there, but I only know a few. I don't think anyone would really want me there since I don't know the person who died. It feels like I'm being forced into a situation where I don't belong. I'm also thinking about the effort it would take. I'm still in college, and this is a big commitment. I don't know if it's worth it for someone I don't know. Plus, my mom has never mentioned this great aunt before, even though she supposedly played a big role in raising her. That makes me question why it's suddenly important now. I'm feeling guilty because my mom is trying to guilt-trip me. She said she'll go on her own, which made me feel bad. But I don't think I should attend just to make her happy. My feelings and comfort matter too. In the end, I don't see how attending would benefit me or the family. It feels more like an obligation without any real connection. So, I'm leaning towards not going, even though it might upset my mom. I think it's more important to respect my own feelings and boundaries.
